promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: The knee comes before the build this week, so I am swapping Wednesday's tempo for cross-training and shortening the long run until a physio has looked at it. Keep every run flat and pain-free, and stop if the sharp pain comes back.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I am not able to diagnose what the pain is, and I would not want to guess between IT band, meniscus or something else from a check-in. Lateral knee pain that is sharp on downhills, worse the next day on stairs, and strong enough to make you walk home is worth a physio visit this week. Please book one.

No on Wednesday's tempo. Hard running on a sore knee is the fastest way to turn a two-week problem into a six-week one, and we have time to protect the race. I have replaced it with 40 minutes of easy cross-training on the bike or in the pool, which keeps the aerobic work going without the downhill loading that set it off.

new.analysis:
## How the week went

You followed the plan Monday through Saturday, hit the paces on the tempo cleanly, and only the long run broke down when the knee flared at mile 7. Walking home from 8.5 instead of forcing 13 was the right decision, and I would make the same call every time.

## Why next week looks like this

The race is 10 weeks out, which is enough runway to lose a quality session and still arrive fit, so I am spending that runway on the knee. Volume drops from 32 to about 19 flat miles, the tempo becomes easy cross-training, and the long run is capped at 8 mi on a flat route with a hard rule to stop if the sharp pain comes back. If a physio clears you mid-week and the knee is quiet, we hold the plan anyway and rebuild quality the following week.

## What I want to see

Flat routes only, no downhill repeats, and a daily note on how the knee feels on stairs the morning after each run. If stairs are pain-free for three days in a row and the Sunday long run goes clean, I will add a short marathon-pace block back the week after. If pain is the same or worse by Thursday, we drop Sunday to easy cross-training and reassess.

safetyCallouts.title: See a physio about the right knee.
safetyCallouts.body: New lateral knee pain that is sharp on downhills, limited you to a walk home, and now aches going down stairs is worth a hands-on assessment this week. Please stop any run if that sharp pain returns, and do not push through it. If it swells, gives way, or you cannot bear weight, treat that as more urgent.
